title: East Africa Commodity Market Prices — Guide for Smallholders
content:
## East Africa Agricultural Commodity Price Guide

*Note: Prices are indicative ex-farm averages. Actual prices vary by region, season, and year. Data reflects 2024–2025 season patterns.*

### Maize

| Market | Low Season (Mar–Jul) | High Season (Aug–Feb) |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------|
| Kenya (Nairobi) | KES 35–45/kg | KES 50–70/kg |
| Kenya (Nakuru) | KES 30–40/kg | KES 45–60/kg |
| Tanzania (Dar es Salaam) | TZS 400–550/kg | TZS 600–900/kg |
| Uganda (Kampala) | UGX 700–900/kg | UGX 1,100–1,500/kg |

**Market tips for maize:**
- Sell during dry season (August–November) for best prices
- Storage for 3–4 months after harvest can double farm income
- NCPB (Kenya) buys at strategic reserve price — check current procurement price
- WFP and NGO purchasing programs exist in food-insecure areas

### Beans (Rose Coco/Red Kidney)

| Market | Low Season | High Season |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| Kenya (Nairobi) | KES 80–120/kg | KES 150–220/kg |
| Tanzania (Arusha) | TZS 1,500–2,200/kg | TZS 2,500–4,000/kg |
| Uganda (Kampala) | UGX 2,500–3,500/kg | UGX 4,000–6,000/kg |

**Market tips for beans:**
- Beans have the best price-to-input-cost ratio of any staple
- Clean, graded beans (uniform size, no broken/discolored) fetch 20–40% premium
- Urban supermarkets pay premium for packaged, graded beans
- Export market: Rwanda and DRC absorb large volumes of East African beans

### Tomatoes

| Market | Off-peak (abundant) | Peak shortage |
|--------|--------------------|--------------|
| Kenya (Nairobi) | KES 15–30/kg | KES 80–150/kg |
| Tanzania (Dar) | TZS 300–600/kg | TZS 1,200–2,500/kg |
| Tanzania (Arusha wholesale) | TZS 400–800/kg | TZS 1,500–3,000/kg |

**Tomato market reality:**
- Extremely volatile — prices swing 5–10x between peak and off-season
- Plan plantings to harvest during Jun–Aug or Nov–Dec for best prices
- Major losses from glut (everyone plants same season)
- Consider contract farming with processors and hotel/restaurant buyers in Arusha/Moshi

### Cassava

| Form | Kenya (Coast) | Tanzania |
|------|--------------|----------|
| Fresh roots | KES 15–25/kg | TZS 200–400/kg |
| Dried flour (dona) | KES 50–80/kg | TZS 800–1,200/kg |

**Value addition:** Processing cassava to flour or chips multiplies price 3–4x. Simple sun-drying equipment costs under USD 50.

### Accessing Better Markets

1. **Farmer cooperatives:** Join or form a group to aggregate produce and negotiate bulk prices
2. **Market information:** Check local radio and agronomy SMS services for daily prices before selling
3. **Post-harvest storage:** PICS bags (hermetic) for grain storage cost ~USD 2 and can store grain 6+ months
4. **Direct sales:** Urban consumer markets, supermarkets, and restaurants often pay 30–50% more than wholesale

## Mwongozo wa Bei za Mazao Afrika Mashariki

*Bei ni za wastani wa shambani. Zinatofautiana kulingana na eneo, msimu, na mwaka.*

### Mahindi

- Kenya (Nairobi): KES 35–70/kg
- Tanzania (Dar): TZS 400–900/kg

**Ushauri wa masoko:** Uza wakati wa kiangazi (Agosti–Novemba) kwa bei nzuri. Kuhifadhi miezi 3–4 kunaweza kuongeza mapato mara mbili.

### Maharagwe

- Kenya (Nairobi): KES 80–220/kg
- Tanzania (Arusha): TZS 1,500–4,000/kg

### Nyanya

- Arusha (jumla): TZS 400–3,000/kg kulingana na msimu
- Bei nzuri Juni–Agosti na Novemba–Desemba

title: Tomato Market Reality — Arusha Commercial Growers
content:
## Realistic Tomato Prices for New Commercial Growers near Arusha

### What a first-season grower should expect (ex-farm, 2024–2025 patterns)

| Grade / Channel | Typical price (TZS/kg) | Notes |
|-----------------|------------------------|-------|
| Farm-gate unsorted (glut) | 300–600 | High volume, low margin |
| Farm-gate unsorted (shortage) | 1,200–2,500 | Short windows only |
| Arusha wholesale graded | 500–1,000 (glut) / 1,500–3,000 (shortage) | Size-sorted, firm fruit |
| Hotels / restaurants (contract) | +20–40% over wholesale | Requires consistent weekly supply |
| Processing / paste | Often below fresh wholesale | Only if fresh market collapses |

**Realistic planning price for a new 2-acre irrigated farm:** budget on **TZS 600–900/kg** average across the season, not peak shortage prices. Peak prices are real but brief.

### Yield × price math (2 acres ≈ 0.8 ha)

- Conservative irrigated yield: 20–30 t/ha → ~16–24 tonnes total
- At TZS 700/kg average: roughly TZS 11–17 million gross before costs
- Seed, fertilizer, chemicals, labour, and transport often take 40–60% — plan cash carefully

### How to get a better price

1. **Grade:** Separate large red ripe, medium, and processing grade
2. **Harvest cool:** Early morning; shade crates; do not stack more than 3 layers
3. **Sell same day** when possible — tomatoes lose firmness fast without cold chain
4. **Stagger planting** every 2–3 weeks so you are not dumping the whole farm in one glut week
5. **Pre-agree** with 1–2 buyers (Tengeru / Arusha central market traders, hotels) before peak harvest

### Currency note

For cross-border comparison: Kenya farm-gate tomato often KES 30–80/kg in normal seasons and KES 80–150/kg in shortage — similar volatility to Tanzania.
content_sw:
## Bei Halisi za Nyanya — Wakulima wa Biashara Arusha

### Bei za kawaida (TZS/kg, shambani)

- Wakati wa wingi: 300–600
- Wakati wa uhaba: 1,200–2,500
- Jumla Arusha (zilizopangwa): 500–3,000 kulingana na msimu

**Bei ya kupanga bajeti (mkulima mpya):** wastani **TZS 600–900/kg** — usitegemee bei ya uhaba pekee.

### Hesabu (ekari 2 ≈ hekta 0.8)

- Mavuno ya tahadhari kwa umwagiliaji: tani 20–30/hekta
- Kwa TZS 700/kg: mapato ya jumla yanaweza kuwa TZS milioni 11–17 kabla ya gharama

### Jinsi ya kupata bei bora

1. Panga matunda kwa ukubwa na ubora
2. Vuna asubuhi; weka kivulini
3. Uza siku ile ile inapowezekana
4. Panda kwa hatua kila wiki 2–3
5. Kubaliana na wanunuzi kabla ya mavuno
